label: copy-phase input y (fed-back y, not the first copied token)
explanation: Token detector for y being fed back as input during the copy phase. Fires on essentially every copy-phase step whose input is y (rate ~1.0 when recall_idx >= 2), i.e. right after the model has emitted a y and is now outputting the token that followed y. Never fires in the original phase (even on y inputs) or at the delimiter step, and never on any other input token. When y is the first original token (input y at recall_idx 1, the first fed-back token), it fires only weakly (~0.01-0.08 of max) or not at all; these are the only misses. Magnitude is lower when y is copied back early (orig position 1-2, ~0.5-0.8 of max) and highest for y at original positions 3+ (~0.8-1.0); repeated y in a row gets slightly smaller on the second. Independent of which token is being output next.

issues: I found no systematic counterexample. On test, the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.979, F1 0.990, mass recall 0.999 and correlation 0.988. Misses on test produced 0 false positives.

Every test miss is a fed-back y at recall_idx 1 (y was the first original token), firing weakly at 0.01-0.06 of max. On test, the y & recall_idx==1 slice has precision 0.094, so about 9% of those steps fire, and it holds 0.08% of activation mass. This matches the explanation's stated exception.

The phase claims check out on dev. The feature fires 0 times in the original phase, 0 times at the delimiter step, and only in the copy phase. Input y accounts for 76210 of 76211 active steps; the single exception is one activation on input v, which is noise.

The magnitude claims match the examples. A y from original position 1 (recall_idx 2) sits around 0.46-0.70 of max, position 2 around 0.7-0.85, and position 3 and later around 0.8-1.0. A second y in a row is somewhat lower (0.81-0.90). Output token and next_out are flat, consistent with 'which token is being output next has no effect'.

Minor wording point: the label says 'not the first copied token'. It would be more precise to say the feature excludes y fed back at recall_idx 1, meaning y as the first original token, rather than y as the first token output. The meaning is the same.
